title: DRVs, RNI and RDA
welcome_lead: How much do we need? UK and EU recommendations explained.
meta_desc: A-Level Food Tech: Dietary Reference Values, RNI and RDA.

concepts.def: Dietary Reference Value — UK family of nutrient intake estimates (COMA 1991).
Reference Nutrient Intake — meets needs of 97.5% of UK population.
Estimated Average Requirement — meets 50% of population needs.
Lower Reference Nutrient Intake — meets only 2.5% of population.
Recommended Daily Allowance — EU labelling reference; replaced by NRV.
Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition (UK), since 2000.

walkthroughs.body_html: The UK DRV system (COMA report, 1991) defines: EAR (50% of population needs), RNI (97.5%), and LRNI (2.5% — risk-of-deficiency floor). SACN (since 2000) updates them.
EU food labelling historically used RDA. Since 2014, EU Regulation 1169/2011 uses Nutrient Reference Value (NRV) — a single reference for adult labelling.
To assess a diet: compare each nutrient intake against RNI. Persistent intakes below LRNI indicate deficiency risk. RNI suits planning; LRNI suits surveillance.
